identity.name: Kingdom of Vientiane
native_names: ອານາຈັກວຽງຈັນ

land.text: the central and southern part of Lan Xang, which kept Vientiane after the partition of 1707

predecessors.note: The kingdom 'was formed in 1707 as a result of the split of the Lan Xang kingdom'; Luang Prabang took the north (kingdom-of-luang-phrabang) and Champasak seceded in the following years (kingdom-of-champasak).

land.text: the Vientiane shape, annexed by Siam in 1828

successors.note: Infobox successor: Rattanakosin Kingdom. 'The Kingdom of Vientiane was obliterated. The Khorat Plateau was formally annexed by Siam' (1828). Vietnam under the Nguyen later annexed Muang Phuan and the provinces of Khammouane and Savannakhet (undated on the page); the nguyen-dynasty and rattanakosin-kingdom dossiers carry that.

capitals.name: Vientiane (Viangchan)
capitals.note: Infobox: capital Vientiane. Sacked in 1779 and burned to the ground in 1827-1828 ('the city was burned to the ground ... its population completely relocated').

rulers.name: Ong Bun (Ong Boun)
rulers.note: First reign; Burmese vassal from 1765. The Siamese sacked Vientiane in 1779 and he was executed in 1781.

rulers.name: Phraya Supho
rulers.note: The infobox list overlaps Ong Bun's first reign by a year.

rulers.name: Nanthasen
rulers.note: Made king by Siam; accused in 1795 of plotting a rebellion with the Lao governor of Nakhon Phanom.

rulers.name: Anouvong (Chao Anu)
rulers.note: Led the rebellion of 1826-1828, captured and caged in Bangkok.

correction.text: the Vientiane shape of 1709 from the founding in 1707

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1707-1708: the page dates the kingdom to 1707, Cliopatria's first shape to 1709. The 1709 shape applies from the founding.

1709-1774, 172,393 km2 (591 cells): Bolikhamxai, Khammouan, Savannakhet and Vientiane, and the Khorat Plateau of Thailand from Nong Khai and Udon Thani to Surin and Ubon Ratchathani. The page names no boundary: it has the kingdom's centre at Vientiane, Nong Khai 'administering the central region' after 1828 and the Khorat Plateau as its field of rebellion. The infobox gives no area. Muang Phuan (Xiangkhouang) is drawn in Luang Prabang's shape, consistently with 'Muang Phuan became a tributary state of Luang Prabang' (Luang Prabang page); the Burmese suzerainty of 1765-1779 is a vassal tint of the Burmese dossier, not a change of shape.
1775-1777: same outline (172,608 km2). Nothing in the page moves a border in these years; the Burmese suzerainty continues and ends with the Siamese sack of 1779.

1778-1787: same outline (172,393 km2). 1778-1779 is the Siamese conquest: 'King Taksin sent General Phraya Chakri ... to attack Vientiane', Vientiane fell in March 1779 (Thonburi infobox) and became a Siamese dependency; the contest is in the ledger, the shape stays Vientiane's (the Siamese made the kingdom a client, not an annexation).
1788-1795: same outline. In 1791 Vientiane was invaded by the Tây Sơn 'to root out Lê dynasty loyalists' (no land changed hands).
1796-1824, 172,157 km2: same outline under Inthavong (1795-1805) and Anouvong (1805-1828).

1825-1827: same outline; Anouvong's rebellion is the contest of December 1826 - 1828. Cliopatria ends the row in 1827, but the page has the kingdom 'obliterated' in 1828 ('the capital remained the largest city of the Lao ... until 1828'), so a new keyframe holds the shape for 1828.

correction.text: the 1825 outline for the year of the annexation, 1828

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1828: Vientiane is destroyed and annexed in this year (the end of the kingdom); the outline of 1825 holds up to the annexation.

region.text: the Vientiane shape: central Laos from Vientiane to Savannakhet and the Khorat Plateau of north-east Siam

ledger.note: 1707: the Kingdom of Vientiane is formed. It 'was formed in 1707 as a result of the split of the' Lan Xang kingdom (the page's wording), with Setthathirath II first on the throne; Kitsarat's Luang Prabang was crowned in the same year.

region.text: the old Lan Xang, divided between Luang Prabang and Vientiane

ledger.note: 1707: Lan Xang divides into Vientiane and Luang Prabang. 'led to the kingdom of Lan Xang being ultimately divided into constituent kingdoms in 1707' (History of Laos page, citing Lan Xang). Champasak follows in the next years (page undated).

region.text: the Vientiane shape: central Laos from Vientiane to Savannakhet and the Khorat Plateau of north-east Siam

ledger.note: 1778: Taksin's Siamese armies invade Laos. 'After Phra Vo's death, Taksin launched the invasion of Laos'; Surasi captured Champasak and the Phra Bang image was taken 'in 1778'; Phraya Chakri marched on Vientiane ('King Taksin sent General Phraya Chakri (the later King Rama I) to attack Vientiane', Vientiane page).

region.text: the Vientiane shape: central Laos from Vientiane to Savannakhet and the Khorat Plateau of north-east Siam

ledger.note: March 1779: Vientiane falls to Siam. 'In 1779, Siamese forces sacked Vientiane, the city was looted with several important Buddha images'; 'King Ong Boun decided to submit to the Siamese and Vientiane became a Siamese dependency'; he was executed in 1781. The Burmese suzerainty of 1765-1779 ends (Vientiane page: 'a Burmese vassal from 1765 to 1779'). About ten thousand Lao were deported (Thonburi page).

December 1826: Anouvong's rebellion. 'In December 1826, Uparat Tissa led his forces' to take Kalasin; 'In mid-January [1827], Anouvong led his forces to take Nakon Ratchasima without resistance'; the Lao armies of Vientiane and Champasak moved across the Khorat Plateau as far as Saraburi (Lao rebellion page).

1828: the rebellion is crushed. 'In 1827, Vientiane was ravaged for a second time by the Siamese armies'; 'By 1828, Anouvong had been captured, tortured and sent to Bangkok' (History of Laos page); 'The Khorat Plateau was formally annexed by Siam.'

region.text: the Vientiane shape of 1825, the kingdom and the Khorat Plateau annexed by Siam

ledger.note: 1828: the Kingdom of Vientiane is obliterated. 'The Kingdom of Vientiane was obliterated. The Khorat Plateau was formally annexed by Siam. The city was burned to the ground and was looted of nearly all treasures, its population completely relocated.' Anouvong was caged until his death; the central region was administered from Nong Khai.

wars.name: Burmese conquest of the Lao kingdoms
wars.outcome: Vientiane's Ong Boun invited the Burmese against Luang Prabang in October 1764; Nemyo Thihapate 'conquered Lao kingdoms of Luang Prabang and Vientiane in March 1765' and both became Burmese vassals ('a Burmese vassal from 1765 to 1779').
wars.note: No land changed hands; the vassal tint belongs to the Burmese dossier (konbaung-dynasty ledger, March 1765).

wars.name: Luang Prabang-Vientiane war and Burmese intervention
wars.outcome: 'In 1773, Luang Prabang forces attacked Vientiane. Ong Bun then sought Konbaung help, which made Vientiane a Burmese vassal.' (The same page dates the vassalage from 1765.)

wars.name: Siamese conquest of Vientiane and Champasak

zones.text: the Vientiane shape: central Laos from Vientiane to Savannakhet and the Khorat Plateau of north-east Siam

wars.outcome: Surasi took Champasak and the Phra Bang in 1778; Vientiane fell in March 1779 and became a Siamese dependency; Ong Boun was executed in 1781 and Nanthasen made king.
wars.note: Thonburi page: the governor of Nangrong rebelled with Champasak's support in 1777 and Chakri was sent to retaliate.

wars.name: Tây Sơn invasion of Vientiane
wars.outcome: 'In 1791, Vientiane was invaded by the Vietnamese Tây Sơn dynasty to root out Lê dynasty loyalists'; Nanthasen later reached an accommodation with the Tây Sơn. No border moved.

wars.name: Lao rebellion (1826-1828)
wars.outcome: Siamese victory: Vientiane was destroyed and annexed in 1828 and its population moved to the Khorat Plateau; Siam consolidated control over Vientiane and Champasak.
wars.note: Anouvong took Nakhon Ratchasima in January 1827; the Lao camped at Mun Kheng on 21 March 1827 and Lomsak fell on 2 April 1827.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line: the borders with Luang Prabang, Champasak and Cambodia are approximate, and the Khorat Plateau part of the shape is a Cliopatria outline that no page opened bounds.

notes:
Page budget 5; five pages opened (WebFetch summaries, so every quotation is the summariser's quotation). None gives an area for the kingdom, so the infobox comparison could not be made; Cliopatria's shape is 172,000 km2.

Cliopatria's six shapes are the same outline, 1709-1827 (Vientiane, Khammouan, Savannakhet, Bolikhamxai and the Khorat Plateau to Surin and Ubon), with differences of a few cells; they are all marked ok. The row starts two years late (1709, the page has 1707) and ends a year early (1827, the page has 1828).

The Burmese suzerainty (1765-1779) and the Siamese suzerainty (1779-1828) are vassal tints that belong to the konbaung-dynasty and thonburi-kingdom/rattanakosin-kingdom dossiers (this state is the vassal, and a vassal records no vassal event of its own). The Vientiane page contradicts itself on 1707: it dates Kitsarat's separation of Luang Prabang to both 1707 and 1779; I use 1707. The Lan Xang partition and Champasak's secession (1713 in the champasak dossier; the Vientiane page gives no year) are other dossiers' events.

Tây Sơn: the Vientiane page dates their invasion to 1791 (the Quang Trung page leaves it undated). Muang Phuan (Xiangkhouang): a tributary of Luang Prabang, drawn in that kingdom's shape. After 1828 Vietnam annexed Muang Phuan, Khammouane and Savannakhet (undated on the page).
